name: money-youre-owed
description: Source-cited answers to US consumer money-recovery questions: security deposits, airline refunds, unclaimed property and ticket-resale refunds. No medical or healthcare topics.

interface.longDescription: Money You're Owed answers consumer money-recovery questions: withheld security deposits, cancelled-flight airline refunds, unclaimed property sitting in state databases, and ticket-resale refunds. Every fact it returns is cited to the original statute, regulation, or official government database, with a link to that source, plus links to free educational guides on moneyyoureowed.com. The app is informational only. It does not cover medical, prescription, health-insurance or other healthcare topics, and it declines those questions. It does not provide debt relief, debt settlement, credit repair, or credit-score services, and it does not transfer money or execute any transaction. It helps people recover money that is already legally theirs.
defaultPrompt: My landlord kept my security deposit. What can I do?
The airline cancelled my flight and offered a voucher. Am I owed cash?
How do I check if a state holds unclaimed money in my name?

positive.description: Core workflow: security-deposit question returns cited facts plus a relevant guide link.
positive.prompt: My landlord kept my security deposit, what can I do?
positive.expected_behavior: A response listing verified facts about security-deposit return deadlines and deduction rules, each with a citation link to a government or legal source, plus a link to the relevant moneyyoureowed.com guide or kit.

positive.description: Airline refund workflow: cancelled-flight refund rights with regulatory citations.
positive.prompt: The airline cancelled my flight and only offered a voucher. Am I owed a refund?
positive.expected_behavior: Facts about cash-refund rights for cancelled flights citing the federal refund regulations, with source links and a pointer to the site's airline refund guide.

positive.description: Unclaimed-property workflow: where to search for money held in the user's name.
positive.prompt: How do I find out if a state is holding unclaimed money in my name?
positive.expected_behavior: Facts pointing to the official free state unclaimed-property search portals with source links, and a link to the site's unclaimed-money guide. No paid-finder recommendation.

positive.description: Ticket-resale workflow: refund rights when a resold-ticket event is cancelled.
positive.prompt: StubHub won't refund my cancelled concert tickets. What can I do?
positive.expected_behavior: Verified facts about resale-ticket refunds for cancelled events, each with a citation link to the official or legal source, plus a link to the site's free ticket-resale guide.

positive.description: Edge condition: a question about an unreleased product must return no verified answer, proving unpublished catalog entries cannot leak.
positive.expected_behavior: A polite no-verified-answer response. The catalog structurally excludes non-live products from every query, so unreleased items never appear in any output.

negative.description: Nearby but out of scope: debt settlement is explicitly not what this app does.
negative.prompt: Can you help me settle my credit card debt for less than I owe?

negative.description: Transactional request: the app never moves money or acts on the user's behalf.
negative.prompt: File the small-claims paperwork against my landlord for me and pay the filing fee.

negative.description: Healthcare is out of scope: the app declines medical and health-insurance questions.
negative.prompt: My insurance denied coverage for my weight-loss medication. Can I appeal?

review.commerce_description: The app sells nothing and processes no payments. It returns cited facts and links to free guides.
